title: Regressions detected with operator microbenchmarks for Pytorch 2.9_rc1 vs Pytorch2.8
bug_description:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Issue:

There are significant regressions in following ops in compile mode, which have been tracked in CI using the new [operator microbenchmarks](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/e934b6ab4055d0f69d1cd9bd1ee8212ad65f34d1/.github/workflows/operator_microbenchmark.yml) workflow:

| Device | Test Name                                                      | Latency (PyTorch 2.8) [milliseconds] | Latency (PyTorch 2.9-rc) [milliseconds] |
|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|-------------------------------|
| A100   | bmm_B8_M256_N256_K64_cuda_dtypetorch.float32                     | 3.985                      | 10.308                        |
| H100   | bmm_B8_M256_N256_K64_cuda_dtypetorch.float16                     | 0.018                      | 4.595                         |
| A100   | matmul_M256_N512_K512_trans_aFalse_trans_bTrue_cuda_dtypetorch.float16 | 2.766                      | 20.111                        |
| H100   | matmul_M256_N512_K512_trans_aFalse_trans_bTrue_cuda_dtypetorch.float16 | 2.754                      | 11.709                        |
| A100   | mm_M256_N512_K512_cuda_dtypetorch.float16                        | 2.738                      | 10.754                        |
| H100   | mm_M256_N512_K512_cuda_dtypetorch.float32                        | 0.018                      | 3.504                         |

## Repro steps:

Setup operator benchmarks:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/tree/main/benchmarks/operator_benchmark#initial-setup

Command
`python -m benchmark_all_test --device cuda --tag-filter long --use-compile --test-name bmm_B8_M256_N256_K64_cuda_dtypetorch.float32`

### Versions

CI Env: ci-image:pytorch-linux-jammy-cuda12.8-cudnn9-py3-gcc11
pytorch: 2.8, 2.9+cu128_RC1
